title: New-Commerce Commitment Schedule for Microsoft 365 Plans: Windows, Renewal Cutoff and Expiry Periods
content:
Under new-commerce terms, a Microsoft 365 Cloud Subscriptions (CSP) commitment can be undone only within short windows. Renewals follow a fixed cutoff, and an expired subscription passes through two set periods before its data is deleted. The figures below are the same on every plan, and the table lists each plan.

## Windows and renewal settings

| Plan | Cancellation window | Window for reducing licenses added by a seat addition | Refund on in-window reduction or cancellation | Renewal change cutoff | Auto-renew on a new subscription | P1M term may be ended by turning auto-renew off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Microsoft 365 Business Basic | 168 hours | 168 hours | yes | 1 day | on | yes |
| Microsoft 365 F3 | 168 hours | 168 hours | yes | 1 day | on | yes |
| Microsoft 365 Business Standard | 168 hours | 168 hours | yes | 1 day | on | yes |
| Microsoft 365 Business Premium | 168 hours | 168 hours | yes | 1 day | on | yes |
| Microsoft 365 E3 (no Teams) | 168 hours | 168 hours | yes | 1 day | on | yes |
| Microsoft 365 E5 (no Teams) | 168 hours | 168 hours | yes | 1 day | on | yes |

- **Cancellation window**: the hours after the window opens (purchase or renewal) within which the whole subscription may be cancelled or its quantity reduced.
- **Window for reducing added licenses**: the hours after a seat addition within which those added licenses may be reduced.
- **Refund on in-window reduction**: whether licenses reduced inside the window are refunded prorated.
- **Renewal change cutoff**: the days before the renewal date by which scheduled renewal changes must be saved.
- **Auto-renew on a new subscription**: the auto-renew setting on a new subscription unless the order form says otherwise.
- **P1M ended by turning auto-renew off**: whether a P1M term may be ended at its next cycle end by turning off auto-renew after the window.

## After expiry

| Plan | Access period after expiry | Administrator-only retention after the access period |
|---|---|---|
| Microsoft 365 Business Basic | 30 days | 90 days |
| Microsoft 365 F3 | 30 days | 90 days |
| Microsoft 365 Business Standard | 30 days | 90 days |
| Microsoft 365 Business Premium | 30 days | 90 days |
| Microsoft 365 E3 (no Teams) | 30 days | 90 days |
| Microsoft 365 E5 (no Teams) | 30 days | 90 days |

- **Access period**: the days after expiry during which users keep access before the subscription is disabled.
- **Retention**: the days after the access period during which only administrators can reach the data before deletion.

## The windows in elapsed time

168 hours is seven full days of elapsed time. Example with hypothetical times: a window that opens at 09:00 on a Monday closes at 09:00 on the following Monday. A seat addition submitted at 14:30 on a Wednesday opens its own window for those added licenses, which closes at 14:30 on the following Wednesday.
